newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo gold futures end firmer, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo gold futures end firmer, others mixed.

text.p: Tokyo gold futures ended slightly firmer on Thursday in relatively volatile trade, moving in line with the currency market, while other precious metals settled mixed, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from unchanged to three yen per gram higher. Benchmark August finished one yen firmer at 1,378 yen.
Buoyant two-way trade was detected. Local investors liquidated their longs in nearby months, while those with short positions bought back, the traders said.
Bullion was quoted at $383.65/95 per ounce at the Tokyo close, against $383.60/384.10 in New York on Wednesday.

In the bullion market, Australian producer selling dented spot gold earlier in the day, but buying by Japanese trade houses and overseas funds, combined with healthy physical demand in Asia, helped gold rebound from early lows.
Traders said gold was likely to consolidate around $383.50 per ounce bofore firming further.
Open interest in gold futures fell to 353,892 lots as of Wednesday, down from 370,220 lots as of October 15.
"Despite recent price gains, fresh buying interest by private investers remained limited, which was reflected in the continued fall in open interest," one trader said.
Platinum futures were up, following gains in New York overnight, while palladium were weaker, pressured by easier spot palladium prices.
Platinum futures ranged from unchanged to six yen per gram firmer. Benchmark August was unchanged at 1,391 yen.
Palladium futures ranged from unchanged to five yen per gram down. Benchmark August was down one at 429 yen.
Silver futures ranged from 0.3 yen per 10 grams lower to 0.6 yen firmer. Benchmark August was flat at 183.0 yen.
